study_identification_part.si_4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with First-Episode Psychosis Using Normative Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis) study was used for the longitudinal clinical sample. The pre-trained normative model was estimated using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites (40,435 participants). The specific dataset names for the pre-training data are not listed in the paper; reference 29 (Wolfers et al.) is cited for the normative model reference datasets.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited to a specific first-episode sub-study of the TOP study at the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital... Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites)."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Berthet2025.pdf.md: Methods / Participants, L31-33; Normative Modeling, L47

answer.TOP: clinical transfer/test set for patients (SCZ) and controls (CTRL); adaptation of normative model to 3 Oslo scanners

answer.MULTI-DATASET (UNSPECIFIED OR N>=10): pre-training of reference normative models (77 sites, 40,435 participants)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The pre-trained normative models were estimated on pooled public datasets (95% train, 5% validation). These models were then adapted (transferred) to 3 unseen Oslo scanners using held-out cross-sectional CTRL data from TOP. Finally, the adapted models were applied to the longitudinal TOP sample (CTRL and SCZ) to compute deviation scores.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites). We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners, by transferring the (hyper)parameters as informed priors for these new sites. For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners... After this transfer step, we tested the normative models on the remaining longitudinal CTRL and SCZ samples."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model was pre-trained on pooled data from 77 sites. Training phase used 40,435 participants (95% of pooled data = healthy individuals for training). Validation used 2,548 participants (5% including both CTRL and patients). Total pooled data: 40,435 + 2,548 = 42,983. For adaptation to Oslo scanners, additional CTRL were used (103 + 294 + 393 = 790 from Supplementary Table 1). The TOP longitudinal analysis included 218 CTRL at baseline, 197 at 12 months, and 77 at 10 years.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites)." Supplementary Table 1 shows adaptation samples: TOP15 n=103, TOP3T n=294, TOP3T-GE n=393.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Berthet2025.pdf.md: Methods / Normative Modeling, L47; media-1.pdf.md: Supplementary Table 1, L133-140

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: For the pre-training dataset (40,435 participants from 77 sites), age statistics are not reported in this paper. For the TOP adaptation sample, Supplementary Table 1 provides mean ages for each scanner: TOP15 36.6 [10.3], TOP3T 31.2 [7.7], TOP3T-GE 33.3 [11.1]. Weighted mean = (36.6*103 + 31.2*294 + 33.3*393)/(103+294+393) = 34.40. Age range for healthy controls is stated as 13-56 years in supplementary methods.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: For the pre-training dataset (40,435 participants from 77 sites), sex statistics are not reported in this paper. For the TOP adaptation sample (n=790), Supplementary Table 1 provides sex ratio (male) for each scanner: TOP15 42.7% male, TOP3T 48.8% male, TOP3T-GE 49.8% male. Weighted male percentage = (42.7*103 + 48.8*294 + 49.8*393)/790 = 47.5%. This corresponds to 375 males and 415 females.
